package_info.package_versions: Unknown (affects Smith & Wesson's deployed version at time of attack)
package_info.why_malicious: The injected code is a malicious JavaScript skimmer designed to steal customer payment data by intercepting and exfiltrating sensitive information entered on the checkout page. This is a classic example of Magecart-style attacks, where attackers exploit web platform vulnerabilities to inject code that harvests credit card and personal data.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into Magento website's checkout page (likely in a .js file or inline script)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the form submission event on the checkout page, collects all form data (including payment details), and exfiltrates it via an HTTP POST request to an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in theft of customer payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating payment form data to an external domain is a hallmark of web skimming attacks and is never legitimate on a payment page.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal e-commerce JavaScript should not send sensitive payment data to third-party domains; it should only submit to the legitimate payment processor.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form data may be sent to payment processors or analytics services, but never full payment details to unknown domains.
key_indicators: Hooks into form submission on sensitive pages
Sends data to external, non-whitelisted domains
Obfuscated or minified code to evade detection

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits a vulnerability in the Magento platform to gain write access to the website's codebase.
Malicious JavaScript skimmer is injected into the checkout page or a loaded JavaScript file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimmer code on customer browsers

attack_chain.action: When a customer submits the checkout form, the skimmer intercepts the data and sends it to the attacker's server.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code hooking into checkout or payment form submission
Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from checkout pages to unrecognized domains
Obfuscated or dynamically injected scripts on sensitive pages
file_indicators: Unexpected changes to checkout page JavaScript files
Inline scripts with event listeners on payment forms
References to external scripts from non-whitelisted domains
network_indicators: POST requests from client browsers to domains not associated with the merchant
Unusual traffic patterns from checkout pages to unknown IPs or domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized JavaScript modifications on checkout/payment pages, especially scripts that hook into form submissions and send data to external domains. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict allowed destinations for form data and scripts. Analyze network traffic from customer browsers for suspicious outbound requests during checkout. Regularly audit web assets for unexpected or obfuscated scripts.
